narrative.overview: MindWeave rejects generic dark-neon AI templates and floating purple-glow card grids in favor of a calm, tactile drafting environment inspired by technical notebooks, cartographic atlases, and disciplined editorial workspaces. Cool putty (#c3d7e5) and pale drafting paper (#edf3f7) establish a glare-free daytime surface where dense concepts remain legible for hours, paired with an optional deep midnight blueprint mode (#0a0d14) for low-light focus.
keyCharacteristics: Dealt cool putty and petrol-teal light palette (swap-pastels) paired with Schibsted Grotesk + JetBrains Mono
Strict zero-violet/lavender palette across all canvas levels, badges, and interactive controls
Single-elevation surfaces using crisp 1px solid borders at rest and directional offset shadow only on focus or hover
4-side directional quadrant handles (Top, Right, Bottom, Left) guaranteeing edges never route through node cards

rules.name: The Zero-Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet, purple, and lavender hues are banned across accents, canvas nodes, gradients, and badge tints.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Job Rule
rules.body: Red, amber, green, and cobalt appear strictly to encode contradiction, partial recall/uniqueness, mastery/consensus, or clickable source anchors.

rules.name: The Tinted Secondary Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary labels on putty or teal surfaces derive from tinted slate (#3f4756) or petrol hue—never pure neutral #888 gray.

rules.name: The Fixed Operate Scale Rule
rules.body: Inside the Spatial Canvas Studio, typography uses fixed rem steps (1.125-1.2x ratio) rather than fluid clamp() scaling so sidebars and canvas cards remain stable across window splits.

rules.name: The Monospace Evidence Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved strictly for timestamps, page numbers, code blocks, Markdown/Mermaid source text, and tabular metrics—never decorative eyebrows.

rules.name: The Single-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Never stack a heavy blurred shadow under an already-bordered resting card; cards use 1px solid borders at rest and lift only on active state or drag.

rules.name: The Directional Quadrant Handle Rule
rules.body: Every Mind Map Node exposes invisible/subtle connection handles on all four edges (Top, Right, Bottom, Left), selected dynamically from parent-child geometry so connector curves always exit cleanly without crossing card bodies.

dos: Do declare elevation once—use crisp 1px solid #aec3d2 borders at rest and apply directional shadow only on hover, selection, or floating overlays.
Do route edges via directional Top/Right/Bottom/Left handles matching the active ELK.js layout (Balanced, Logic Tree, Radial, Flowchart).
Do pair every spatial diagram node with clickable monospace source citations (Page X / ▶ MM:SS) when grounded in uploaded PDFs or YouTube videos.
Do render every view's 5 states (loading skeletons, instructional empty, success, partial error, fatal error) using real studio copy.
donts: Don't use violet, purple, or neon gradients anywhere in node palettes, buttons, or hero backgrounds.
Don't place one-sided vertical accent bars along the left edge of rounded cards; use full 4-side borders, subtle surface tints, or leading badges instead.
Don't place uppercase eyebrow kickers above headings or decorate idle surfaces with blurred frosted glass.
Don't use fake export toasts, disabled placeholder buttons, or generic spinners inside empty content regions.
